title: IP-MT286-EditorInlineGitBlame

scope.summary:
GOAL: Add VS Code / GitLens-class inline git blame to the native code editor — a dim end-of-line annotation on the CURRENT caret line showing 'Author, N time ago • commit summary', plus a hover card with the full commit (author, date, sha, message) and a per-file 'toggle blame' mode that annotates every visible line. The MT-281 matrix marks 'inline-git-blame' MISSING: source_control.rs dispatches a blame DISPLAY event to a panel but there is NO end-of-line inline blame annotation in the editor body. Blame data is fetched via the EXISTING SourceControlClient blame seam (backend_client, the same /source-control blame path source_control.rs already uses) — this MT adds NO new git blame implementation; it adds the inline annotation renderer + hover card + toggle over that existing data.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: (a) NEW module src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/inline_blame.rs (BlameLine, BlameSet, InlineBlameState, the blame client seam consumption, the end-of-line annotation renderer, the hover commit card, AccessKit author_ids); (b) `pub mod inline_blame;` + re-exports in code_editor/mod.rs; (c) wiring in code_editor/panel.rs: fetch blame off-thread on open (and invalidate on save/edit of a line), render the current-line annotation after the line's text glyphs, a hover card on the annotation, a 'Toggle File Blame' chord/command that annotates all visible lines, and the caret-line-follows behavior; (d) one integration test file. NO backend edits (consumes the existing blame route); NO new git blame logic.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. inline_blame.rs: `pub struct BlameLine { line: usize, author: String, author_time_utc: i64, commit_sha: String, summary: String, is_uncommitted: bool }`; `pub struct BlameSet { lines: Vec<BlameLine>, loaded: bool, error: Option<String> }`; `pub struct InlineBlameState { set: BlameSet, file_blame_visible: bool }`. Data comes from the SourceControlClient blame seam, not recomputed.
2. Current-line annotation: after the caret line's text, render a dim (theme-token muted color, no hardcoded hex) inline annotation 'Author, relative-time • summary' (relative time formatted from author_time_utc via chrono — 'You, uncommitted' when is_uncommitted). It sits to the RIGHT of the line content, never overlapping the code, and is non-selectable decoration text (not part of the buffer). It updates as the caret moves between lines. A line with no blame (newly added, uncommitted) shows 'You, uncommitted changes' rather than a fabricated commit.
3. Hover card: hovering the annotation (or the line, in file-blame mode) opens a small card with author, full date, short sha, and the commit summary/first body line. The card reuses the existing hover-tooltip mechanism (editor_view HoverTooltip / gutter diagnostic hover precedent). A 'copy sha' affordance is optional but the sha must be visible.
4. Toggle file blame: a 'Toggle File Blame' command/chord annotates EVERY visible line with a compact author+time gutter-adjacent column (VS Code 'Toggle Line Blame' / GitLens file blame). This mode uses the virtualized visible-row set (MT-002) so only visible lines are annotated; scrolling reveals more without recomputing blame (blame is per-file, fetched once).
5. Fetch + invalidation: blame is fetched once per file open, off-thread (HBR-QUIET), drained next frame. Editing a line marks that line's blame stale (annotation switches to 'uncommitted') without re-fetching on every keystroke; an explicit refresh re-fetches. An unavailable blame seam / untracked file leaves BlameSet.loaded=false with a typed reason and renders NO annotation (never guesses authorship — authorship is a correctness-sensitive claim).
6. AccessKit: the current-line annotation is a Role::Label `code_editor_blame_current` (instance-suffixed per panel.rs RISK-004); the hover card `code_editor_blame_card`; in file-blame mode, per-line labels `code_editor_blame_line_{line}`.
7. Scope edge: REUSES the SourceControlClient blame seam + the existing hover mechanism + MT-002 virtualization; does NOT implement blame, does NOT modify source_control.rs, and does NOT own the SCM change bars (those are MT-285).

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read source_control.rs (the Blame display event + how it calls the SourceControlClient blame path) and backend_client.rs (the blame request/response shape — REUSE it), editor_view.rs (HoverTooltip / hover state) + gutter.rs diagnostic-hover precedent, panel.rs (off-thread dispatch + next-frame drain, virtualized visible rows, caret line, RISK-004 instance-suffix ids, per-line paint after text glyphs), virtual_lines.rs (visible row set), keymap.rs (add ToggleFileBlame chord).
2. Create inline_blame.rs with BlameLine/BlameSet/InlineBlameState + the blame client seam consumption + the relative-time formatter (chrono) + the end-of-line annotation renderer + the hover card + AccessKit nodes; unit-test the relative-time format and the uncommitted-line fallback.
3. Wire panel.rs: blame fetch off-thread on open, current-line annotation after the caret line's text, hover card, Toggle File Blame over the visible-row set, caret-follow, edit->stale.
4. Register the module + re-exports in code_editor/mod.rs.
5. Integration test: a file with known blame shows 'Author, time • summary' on the caret line; caret move updates it; hover opens the card with the sha; an edited/uncommitted line shows 'You, uncommitted'; Toggle File Blame annotates all visible lines; an untracked file shows NO annotation with a typed reason. Capture Argus screenshot + AccessKit tree of the current-line annotation, the hover card, and file-blame mode.
6. Update the UserManual (same change): inline blame — the current-line annotation, hover card, Toggle File Blame, uncommitted-line meaning, and untracked-file behavior.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/** (consumes the existing source-control blame route; no backend git changes)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/source_control.rs (the SCM change-list panel is a distinct surface; reuse its blame client path, do not modify it)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/scm_gutter.rs (the change bars are MT-285; blame is a separate decoration)
acceptance_criteria: code_editor/inline_blame.rs exists with BlameLine/BlameSet/InlineBlameState, an end-of-line current-line annotation renderer, a hover commit card, and Toggle File Blame over the MT-002 visible-row set; AccessKit author_ids code_editor_blame_current / code_editor_blame_card / code_editor_blame_line_{line}, instance-suffixed on multi-pane mount.

Blame data comes from the EXISTING SourceControlClient blame seam (grep-provable: no new blame/git implementation in inline_blame.rs); the annotation renders as non-selectable decoration text to the right of the line, never overlapping code, colored from theme tokens (no hardcoded hex).

The current-line annotation shows 'Author, relative-time • summary' and updates as the caret moves; an uncommitted/edited line shows 'You, uncommitted changes' rather than a fabricated commit; the hover card shows author, full date, short sha, and summary.

Blame is fetched off-thread once per file open (HBR-QUIET, no render-thread block); editing a line marks it stale without per-keystroke refetch; an untracked file / unavailable seam renders NO annotation with a typed reason (never guesses authorship).
Toggle File Blame annotates every VISIBLE line using the virtualized row set; scrolling reveals more without re-fetching.
UserManual updated in the same change: current-line annotation, hover card, Toggle File Blame, uncommitted-line meaning, untracked-file behavior.
proof_targets: Argus evidence: argus.screenshot + AccessKit tree of (a) the current-line annotation, (b) the open hover commit card, (c) Toggle File Blame mode, stored under $HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT
code_surfaces: src/frontend/handshake_native/src/code_editor/panel.rs (off-thread fetch + current-line annotation + hover + toggle + caret-follow + edit->stale)
expected_tests: unit: relative-time formatting from author_time_utc (chrono); 'You, uncommitted' fallback for is_uncommitted
unit: annotation renders to the right of line content and is non-selectable decoration (not buffer text)
unit: AccessKit node tree (current annotation + hover card + per-line labels, stable suffixed ids)
integration: caret move updates the current-line annotation to the correct BlameLine
integration: hover opens the card with author/date/sha/summary
integration: edited line switches to 'uncommitted' without a refetch; explicit refresh re-fetches
integration: untracked file / unavailable seam renders no annotation with a typed reason
integration: Toggle File Blame annotates all visible lines; scroll reveals more without refetch
implementation_notes: Verified grounding 2026-07-21: source_control.rs already models a Blame DISPLAY event and calls the SourceControlClient blame path via backend_client (verified /source-control/* routes); editor_view HoverTooltip + gutter diagnostic-hover give the hover-card mechanism; panel.rs paints per-line after text glyphs, owns the caret line + off-thread drain + RISK-004 instance-suffix ids; virtual_lines.rs (MT-002) gives the visible-row set for file-blame mode; chrono is a workspace dep for relative time.

Design basis (cite in code docs): VS Code inline blame (git.blame / 'Toggle Line Blame') + GitLens current-line blame — dim end-of-line 'Author, time ago • summary', a hover with the full commit, and a whole-file blame toggle.

Authorship is a correctness-sensitive claim: NEVER show a guessed author. Uncommitted/edited/untracked lines show an explicit uncommitted/absent state; only real blame-seam data yields an author + sha.

This MT is a SEPARATE decoration from MT-285's change bars: blame is an end-of-line annotation, change bars are gutter markers. They share the SourceControlClient but not the render surface; keep their AccessKit namespaces distinct.
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-290 timeline consumes the same commit history but as a panel; MT-285 change bars are the gutter dirty-diff.

surfaces: Toggle File Blame full-file annotation mode

target_entries: Inline git blame: the current-line author/time/summary annotation, the hover commit card, Toggle File Blame, what 'uncommitted' means, and behavior for untracked files

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Read-only decoration over blame data; emits no new business events.
Blame-load status, per-line staleness, and fetch outcome (loaded / untracked / error) are exposed as structured state so a no-context model can see why an annotation did or did not render.
Render/decoration surface; the off-thread blame fetch is a bounded task, not a supervised child process.

risk_if_missed: Without inline blame an operator or reviewing agent cannot see, at the caret, who last changed a line and why — a core professional-IDE / GitLens affordance that is especially valuable when reviewing agent-authored edits in a worktree session (was this line mine, HEAD's, or the agent's?).

risks: RISK-1: Fabricated authorship — a line with no real blame data shows a guessed author/commit, making a false provenance claim about who wrote code (authority laundering).
RISK-2: Overlap/obscuring — the end-of-line annotation overlaps code, wraps oddly, or (in file-blame mode) obscures the gutter/SCM bars, degrading readability.
RISK-3: Render-thread block — the blame fetch runs synchronously, freezing the editor on a large-history file.
RISK-4: Stale blame after edits — an edited line keeps its old committed author annotation, implying the current text is that commit's when it is not.
RISK-5: AccessKit collision on dual mount — blame annotation ids collide across panes, breaking the Argus/keyboard path.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Annotation renders ONLY from real blame-seam data; untracked/unavailable -> no annotation + typed reason; uncommitted/edited -> explicit 'You, uncommitted'. A test asserts no author string appears without backing blame data.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): The annotation is right-aligned non-selectable decoration that never overlaps line glyphs; an Argus overlap check + a test on a long line confirm no collision and no clash with MT-285 bars.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Blame fetch is off-thread + drained next frame; grep proves no block_on/join on the render path.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Editing a line marks its blame stale and switches the annotation to 'uncommitted'; a test edits a blamed line and asserts the committed author annotation is replaced.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Reuse the panel.rs RISK-004 instance-suffix scheme; a dual-mount test asserts non-colliding blame author_ids.

Confirmed 'inline-git-blame' is not covered by WP-012 (MT-001..108), WP-013/014 stubs, STUDIO, or WP-011. External design basis: VS Code inline blame / GitLens current-line blame.
corrections: Blame exists only as a panel DISPLAY event today; the inline end-of-line annotation + hover card + file-blame toggle are confirmed MISSING and are what this MT adds, reusing the existing blame client seam rather than implementing git blame.
